FaultJunction.description: State schema 16: the plate-boundary junction pulling on a mega (the strongest pull within fault_junction_km).

kind.description: triple: boundaries of 3+ plates meet; knot: a dense, twisting stretch of boundary far from any triple junction.

km.description: Great-circle distance (km) from the aim to it.

name.description: Its name when it is a famous one ("Afar triple junction"): narration says "at the Afar triple junction".

plates.description: PB2002 plate codes meeting there (sorted); empty for a knot.

strength.description: 0..1: the strongest triple junction is 1 (by the size of the plates meeting and the boundary around it).

FaultTier.description: State schema 16: a mega's tier: junction (within fault_junction_km of a junction), fault (≤ fault_near_km from a fault line), near (the first half of the curve), mild (the second half), tiny (≥ fault_far_km: a tiny volcano; its lasting mods stay local).

LonLat.description: [longitude, latitude] in degrees (WGS84). Note the order: longitude first.

description: `game.fault` (state schema 16): what a mega aimed here would get (the hover preview while a mega is armed). Read-only and deterministic.

factor.description: The multipliers a mega gets there under this match's rules (the distance curve, times the junction's).

magnitude.description: Added to the mega's magnitude (rounded when it lands, 1..10).

junction.description: The junction pulling on it, or null (also null before state schema 16 or with fault_junctions_enabled off).

junctions.description: The match's fault rule includes junctions and tiers (state schema 16 and fault_junctions_enabled).

km.description: Great-circle distance (km) to the nearest fault line.

title: game.fault

x-args.description: Over HTTP every arg is a query-string parameter (numbers as numeric strings). Unknown args are ignored.

at.description: [lon, lat] in degrees (over HTTP `at=lon,lat`; or give `lon` and `lat`).

x-description: State schema 16 (the hover preview while a mega is armed): what a mega aimed at `at` would get: great-circle distance to the nearest fault line (`km`), its `tier` (junction, fault, near, mild, tiny), the junction pulling on it (`{name?, kind, at, strength, plates, km}` or null) and the multipliers `factor: {magnitude (added), radius, damage}` under this match's rules. Read-only, deterministic, cheap (reads only the settings).
